name: Torres Blancas
key_features: Concrete tower of clustered cylinders with rounded cantilevered terraces and planted balconies.

name: Villa Bloemenwerf
key_features: Van de Velde's own gabled house, designed with its furniture, fabrics and fittings as one work of art.

name: Bauhaus Dessau
key_features: A pinwheel plan, with a glass curtain wall wrapping the workshops.

name: Bocconi University Urban Campus
key_features: Curving buildings in a park, wrapped in perforated metal skins around open garden courts.

name: Burton Barr Central Library
key_features: Copper-clad desert box; the top reading room's roof hangs on cables, and the north and south walls tune the sun.

name: Curtain Wall House
key_features: A two-storey fabric curtain stands in for the outside wall; drawn back, the living floor opens to the city.

name: Eden Project
key_features: Geodesic biomes of ETFE cushions on hexagonal steel frames set into a clay pit.

name: Brion Cemetery
key_features: Concrete, water and interlocking circles: a lesson in detail and procession.

name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
key_features: Low pavilions and open madang courtyards set between Gyeongbokgung Palace and the old Bukchon streets.

name: Paustian House
key_features: Waterfront showroom whose open hall rises under tree-like columns and roof lights.

name: St. Johann von Capistran
key_features: A round brick church whose flat roof rests on slim columns, with a large skylight over the altar.

name: Stadshal (Market Hall), Ghent
by: Robbrecht en Daem, Marie-José Van Hee
key_features: Open hall of twin steep timber-clad roofs on concrete legs among Ghent's towers; light pierces the wooden ceiling.

name: Barcelona Pavilion
by: Mies van der Rohe, Lilly Reich
key_features: Free-standing walls under a floating roof: space that flows instead of rooms.

name: Centennial Hall, Tokyo Institute of Technology
key_features: A half-cylinder of aluminium cuts diagonally across stacked boxes above a glazed hall.

name: Engel House
key_features: The first building in Tel Aviv lifted on pilotis, freeing the ground for shade and breeze on Rothschild Boulevard.

name: Castelvecchio Museum
key_features: A medieval castle reworked with precise new joints, cuts and display stands.

name: Dudhsagar Dairy
key_features: Exposed concrete towers, silos and halls arranged to follow the flow of milk through the plant.

name: Feynan Ecolodge
key_features: A desert lodge shaped like a caravanserai around a courtyard, lit by hand-made candles at night.

name: Fujisawa Municipal Gymnasium (Akibadai)
key_features: Two arenas under curved stainless-steel roofs, likened to a samurai helmet or a beetle.

name: Gemini Residence
key_features: Two concrete grain silos converted to flats with balconies hung on the outside.

name: Kala Academy
key_features: Pergola-shaded walkways and an open-air amphitheatre beside the Mandovi river.

name: Lister County Courthouse
key_features: Ochre Nordic-classical courthouse with a clock gable and a great arched, fan-glazed entrance.

name: 1111 Lincoln Road
key_features: Parking garage for about 300 cars with an unusual open form; opened 2010.

name: Bordeaux Law Courts
key_features: Cedar-clad courtroom pods shaped like wine vats stand under an undulating roof behind a glass wall.

name: Cité de Refuge (Salvation Army Hostel)
key_features: An entry route of gateway, bridge and drum leads to a long slab whose glass wall later gained brise-soleil.

name: Cranbrook Estate
by: Berthold Lubetkin (with Francis Skinner, Douglas Bailey)
key_features: Six tower blocks in pairs in height order, with a figure-eight street layout.

name: David H. Koch Theater
key_features: Travertine colonnade on Lincoln Center plaza fronts a gilded promenade hall ringed by balconies.

name: Edifício Niemeyer
key_features: Curving apartment tower wrapped in continuous horizontal sun-breaker bands, on Praça da Liberdade.

name: Japan Pavilion, Expo 2000
key_features: A long gridshell of paper tubes under a paper membrane roof, designed to be recycled afterwards.

name: Ningbo History Museum
key_features: Walls laid in 'wapan' from tiles and bricks salvaged from demolished villages.

name: Caja Granada Headquarters
key_features: Concrete cube with a deep gridded sunscreen facade; inside, a vast hall caught by skylights.

name: Church of Saint Anthony of Polana
key_features: Concrete church whose crown of tapering ribs rises to a point, with coloured glass set between them.

name: The Economist Building
key_features: Three buildings of different heights round a raised plaza off St James's Street, clad in Portland stone.

name: Stadthaus Ulm
key_features: White panelled pavilion with curved and glazed corners stands on the square facing Ulm Minster.

name: Churchill College
key_features: Brown brick walls, pre-cast concrete lintels and teak-framed glazing; nine residential courts.

name: Lillington Gardens
by: Darbourne & Darke (Roger Westman, John Darbourne, Geoffrey Darke)
key_features: High density in medium-rise blocks, with private gardens at ground and roof levels.

name: Netherlands Embassy, Berlin
key_features: A continuous route, the 'trajectory', winds up through the cube from entrance to roof terrace.

name: Omotesando Hills
key_features: Spiral ramp around a six-storey triangular atrium continues the slope of the avenue inside.

name: Skovshoved Petrol Station
key_features: Oval concrete canopy on a single slim column floats over the pumps.

name: 22 Parkside (Rogers House)
key_features: Steel portal frames closed by glass ends: a house and a studio either side of a garden court.

name: Academy of Fine Arts Vienna
key_features: Theophil Hansen's Ringstraße academy building of 1877, home to a public art school and its collection.

name: Les Arcades du Lac
key_features: Social housing as a classical garden city: precast concrete arcades and blocks laid out on axes by a lake.

name: Cabanon de Le Corbusier
key_features: A single Modulor-proportioned room inside a log-clad hut on the coast.

name: Church of La Medalla Milagrosa
key_features: Thin hyperbolic paraboloid shells twist into columns and roof as one continuous concrete structure.

name: Villa Tugendhat
key_features: The open plan in a family home, with glass walls that drop away to the garden.

name: Bouça Social Housing
key_features: Parallel rows of stacked duplex homes with outside stairs and galleries, shielded from the railway by a long wall.

name: Sakaide Artificial Ground
key_features: A concrete deck 6 to 9 m up carries public housing and a new ground; shops, halls and parking sit beneath.

name: Aranya Low Cost Housing
key_features: Plots and a service core for 80,000 people, which families extend over time.

name: Casa de Ferro (Iron House)
key_features: Prefabricated house on a wrought-iron frame clad in embossed iron panels; assembled in Maputo in 1892.

name: Cauchie House
key_features: Narrow Art Nouveau town house on a 6 m wide plot; the façade is covered in allegorical sgraffito decoration.

name: El Colegio de México
by: Teodoro González de León, Abraham Zabludovsky
key_features: Bush-hammered concrete blocks with marble chips stepping around a large terraced courtyard.

name: Haystack Mountain School of Crafts
key_features: Cedar-shingled studios with peaked roofs float on piers above a steep slope, along a grand stair down to the sea.

name: Les Orgues de Flandre
key_features: Housing towers that step up and down like organ pipes, named after musical forms.

name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa
key_features: A round glass perimeter with no front, holding the galleries as separate boxes.

name: Capitol Complex
key_features: Vast plaza grouping assembly, high court and secretariat with monuments, pools and earth mounds.

name: Second Artigas House (Residência Vilanova Artigas II)
key_features: Artigas's own house of 1949, built before his concrete houses of the São Paulo school.

name: Casa De Blas
key_features: A light white steel table with a glass box beneath, set on a heavy concrete podium on a hilltop.

name: Bolgatanga Library
key_features: A raised, wing-like roof and perforated block walls let breezes and filtered light into the reading rooms.

name: Chand Baori
key_features: A stepwell thirteen storeys deep: architecture as a climate machine.

name: Banco Borges & Irmão
key_features: Small white bank on a corner, its curved wall turning the street; the first Mies van der Rohe Award.

name: Claudio Santoro National Theatre
key_features: Truncated pyramid whose blind walls carry relief cubes casting shadows, with glazed end facades.

name: Malaysian Houses of Parliament
key_features: Tower with a grid of precast sunscreens beside a low hall under a crown of triangular roofs.

name: Mjostarnet
key_features: An 18-storey glulam frame with large diagonal timber braces, among the tallest timber buildings.

name: The Pyramids (College Life Insurance)
by: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
key_features: Three 11-storey pyramids: blank concrete walls face the highway, sloping glass walls face the lake.

name: Accor Arena (Palais omnisports de Paris-Bercy)
by: Andrault & Parat, Jean Prouvé, Aydin Guvan
key_features: Pyramid-shaped arena whose sloping walls are covered with lawn; seats about 7,000 to 20,300.

name: ADAC Headquarters
key_features: 93 m tower on a rounded, amoeba-like base; its glass skin is a mosaic of 22 colours led by ADAC yellow.

name: AEG Turbine Factory
key_features: Three-hinged steel frames and glazed side walls under a temple-like gable.

name: Amos Rex
key_features: Underground galleries beneath Lasipalatsi square, lit by tiled domes with round skylights you can climb on.

name: Arquipélago Contemporary Arts Centre
by: Menos é Mais Arquitectos, João Mendes Ribeiro
key_features: An 1890s basalt distillery restored and joined by two new concrete buildings for art and performance.

name: Brunswick Centre
key_features: Two long stepped terraces of 560 flats with glazed balconies and service towers, framing a shopping street.

name: Chassé Theater
key_features: A single undulating roof sweeps over fly towers and foyers, gathering several halls into one form.

name: CN Tower
key_features: Y-shaped slip-formed concrete shaft whose three buttressing legs carry the pod and antenna.

name: Petrobras Headquarters (Edise)
key_features: 29-storey brutalist block whose façade spaces link indoor and outdoor areas and shade the sun.

name: Andrew Melville Hall
key_features: Precast concrete residence whose splayed wings step down the slope toward the sea, joined by a glazed walkway.

name: De Rotterdam
key_features: Three stacked, shifted towers form a vertical city of offices, flats and a hotel.

name: Maison de Radio-Canada
key_features: Broadcast headquarters of Radio-Canada's French-language services, completed 1973.

name: Manhattan House
key_features: A 21-storey modern apartment building filling a whole city block, built 1949–51 for New York Life.

name: Margaret Esherick House
key_features: Deep recessed window walls in a plain stucco box; wooden shutters control light and view separately.

name: Marl Town Hall
key_features: Germany's first suspended towers: floors hung from the top of concrete cores, beside a council hall with a folded roof.

name: Murcia Town Hall Extension
key_features: Sandstone facade of irregular piers and openings, like a musical score, facing the cathedral square.

name: Torre de las Telecomunicaciones (Antel Tower)
key_features: Tallest skyscraper in Uruguay, 157.6 m, headquarters of Antel.

name: Asilo Sant'Elia
key_features: Kindergarten around a courtyard, its glazed classrooms shaded by a free concrete frame with awnings.

name: Auditorium Niccolò Paganini
key_features: A disused sugar factory shell opened with glass end walls so the concert hall looks out onto the park.

name: Benesse House Museum
key_features: Concrete galleries cut into a hillside above the sea, combining museum rooms with guest rooms.

name: Beth Sholom Synagogue
key_features: A translucent pyramidal roof on a steel tripod floats over a sloping, column-free sanctuary.

name: Blue Building (Blue Condominium)
key_features: Interwar apartment block on Exarchia Square, its corner wrapped in curved cantilevered balconies.

name: Breuer Building
key_features: Inverted stepped granite block with a trapezoid window, overhanging a sunken sculpture court.

name: Burgo Tower
key_features: Office tower wrapped in a grid of metal bands that reads differently on each face, beside a low block.

name: Casa alle Zattere
key_features: A modern house on the Giudecca canal that reworks the Venetian palazzo: plaster walls, framed windows.

name: Casa das Mudas Art Centre
key_features: Dark basalt volumes set into a cliff top above the sea, with roof terraces and paths through the building.

name: Church of the Light
key_features: A cross cut into a concrete wall: light as the only ornament.

name: Copan Building
key_features: Serpentine slab of over a thousand flats with continuous horizontal sunshades over a public arcade.

name: DeFlat Kleiburg
key_features: A 1970s Bijlmermeer slab of 500 flats saved from demolition; residents buy bare shells and fit them out.

name: Lamune Onsen
key_features: Bathhouse of charred cedar and plaster, with pine trees sprouting from its rooftop towers.

name: Belén Library Park
key_features: Library park in Comuna 16 of Medellín, opened March 2008.

name: Espaces d'Abraxas
key_features: Social housing in prefabricated concrete shaped as a palace, a theatre and an arch.

name: Flower Tower
key_features: Ten storeys wrapped in balconies lined with about 380 concrete pots of bamboo, watered automatically.

name: Hôtel van Eetvelde
key_features: Octagonal hall under a glass cupola lights the core of a narrow townhouse.

name: Maison de la Radio
key_features: A ring of offices nearly 500 m round, with a tall archive tower at its centre, on the bank of the Seine.

name: Norwegian Glacier Museum
key_features: Long concrete block in the valley, with stairs on both sides leading up to a roof viewing deck.
